data.title: Tinea corporis / cruris / faciei — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Tinea corporis / cruris / faciei** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. What are dermatophytes?**
- Keratinophilic fungi of genera Trichophyton, Microsporum and Epidermophyton that infect keratin (skin, hair, nails); anthropophilic, zoophilic, geophilic

**Q2. Clinical features of tinea corporis/cruris?**
- Annular/arcuate plaques with active scaly papulovesicular border and central clearing, itchy; cruris on groins/inner thighs sparing scrotum (unlike candida)
- Indian epidemic: extensive, multiple, concentric (tinea pseudoimbricata), steroid-modified (tinea incognito) lesions, chronic and recurrent

**Q3. What is the current Indian dermatophytosis scenario?**
- Since ~2014 an epidemic of chronic, recurrent, extensive and treatment-resistant tinea driven by Trichophyton indotineae (formerly T. mentagrophytes genotype VIII), misuse of steroid–antifungal combinations, poor adherence and squalene epoxidase mutations (terbinafine resistance)

**Q4. Investigations?**
- KOH mount (10–20%): branching septate hyphae; culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar with chloramphenicol and cycloheximide (DTM); dermoscopy; MALDI-TOF/sequencing and antifungal susceptibility testing in resistant cases

**Q5. Differential diagnosis of annular lesions?**
- Nummular eczema, psoriasis, pityriasis rosea (herald patch), seborrhoeic dermatitis, granuloma annulare (no scale), erythema annulare centrifugum (trailing scale), SCLE, leprosy (anaesthetic), annular lichen planus, Hansen's BT

**Q6. What is tinea incognito?**
- Tinea modified by topical steroids — less scaling, ill-defined border, pustules, extensive spread, Majocchi granuloma

**Q7. What is Majocchi granuloma?**
- Deep perifollicular dermatophyte infection (often T. rubrum) after steroid use or shaving legs; nodules/pustules — needs systemic antifungals

**Q8. What is tinea imbricata?**
- Trichophyton concentricum infection — concentric rings of scale ('tokelau'), Pacific islands; Indian 'pseudoimbricata' pattern due to steroid misuse

**Q9. Treatment (Indian practice)?**
- Topical azole/allylamine (luliconazole, sertaconazole, amorolfine, terbinafine) — continue 2 weeks after clearance
- Systemic for extensive/recurrent: itraconazole 200 mg/day for 4–8 weeks (preferred now in India), terbinafine 250–500 mg/day, griseofulvin, fluconazole; combinations in recalcitrant cases
- General: stop steroids, treat family, loose cotton clothes, wash and dry clothing, avoid sharing

## Quick spotter facts
- Annular scaly plaque with active border and central clearing — tinea corporis

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Superficial fungal infection); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.18; ECTODERM/IADVL consensus on dermatophytosis. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
